learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant established analytical, computational and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Applies mechanical knowledge to the study of human body movement.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

teaching_methods: Participatory classroom presentations of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Workshops, debates, seminars, case studies, role-playing, etc.
Development, writing, and presentation of reports, studies, audiovisual material, etc., related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense

assessment_rules: Individual written and oral tests have recovery mechanisms of the same type. The project-based assessment has no recovery mechanisms. The overall grading formula and minimum pass marks are not explicitly stated for the combination of the different assessment components.
